analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: Torah 92 is an extremely brief practical instruction that refers back to LM1 Torah 205 for the full conceptual elaboration. The text discusses several concepts — קְלִפָּה (the klipa), פְּגָם (the spiritual blemish from מִקְרֵה לַיְלָה), מִקְרֵה לַיְלָה (nocturnal emission), מָשִׁיחַ (Mashiach), and נִדְחֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (scattered Israel) — but none are joined to other concepts through explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת / נִקְרָא / הוּא). The relationship between the ten melodies and the klipa is stated as oppositional (הֶפֶךְ — the opposite of) and functional (כֹּחַ לְבַטֵּל — power to nullify), both of which are eitza/oppositional in nature rather than bechina. The relationship between the ten chapters and the tikkun (תִּקּוּן לְמִקְרֵה לַיְלָה) is recorded as a separate eitza edge in the dataset, correctly classified. No bechina concepts are present in the source text that are absent from the dataset.
